summary: UI validation relies on screenshot probes for the menu, room start, combat, and post-card states so layout changes can be judged visually even in headless-first sessions.

UI regressions should be checked with screenshot probes for combat, targeting, after-play, the camp menu, and pile inspectors, because key overlays are built in code and scene-instantiation tests alone will miss visual breakage.

Block behavior is codified in regression tests: player block must absorb damage across the whole enemy phase, and enemy block must persist into the next player turn until it is spent by incoming damage or cleared when that enemy acts again.
The reaver idle sheet is exported column-major (top-to-bottom, then left-to-right), so CombatBoardView must reorder frames instead of using the default row-major atlas order.
archived_reason: Atlas analysis and in-engine playback verification showed the smoothest 8-frame idle loop is standard row-major order.

summary: CombatBoardView overrides the final frame of player_reaver_idle with the penultimate frame because the exported last pose makes the sword pop abruptly in motion.
CombatBoardView plays player_reaver_idle as a ping-pong loop (0..7..1) so the idle bob reverses cleanly instead of snapping from the last pose back to the first.
archived_reason: Ping-pong looping did not improve the perceived hitch enough to keep, so CombatBoardView was reverted to the straightforward forward row-major idle loop.

summary: Per-enemy sprite sizing is driven by enemy_def art_scale and applied after fitting the texture, scaling around the fitted rect center so smaller variants stay tile-centered and keep their HUD alignment.

RunEngine traversal is now a sealed ring graph: non-center rooms keep east/west same-depth links, only one quarter of each ring links deeper, and move filtering permanently blocks any room once you leave it or any exit toward lower depth.
CombatBoardView auto-loads same-stem _idle sheets into 4x2 frame loops and only uses those frames when a unit is not currently being moved or focused by combat presentation.
CombatBoardView idle sheets are now data-driven per unit: definitions can override idle_sheet_columns, idle_sheet_rows, and idle_sheet_order while same-stem _idle loading remains automatic.
details: Default behavior stays 4x2 row-major, but Ash Acolyte uses 2x4 column_major and is covered by _test_acolyte_idle_sheet_honors_column_major_layout in tests/run_tests.gd.

summary: Combat board door visibility is presentation-driven, not layout-driven.
details: Room layouts still stamp door blockers into the grid for topology/pathing, but the board renderer shows a wall unless the tile is an active exit or a sealed previously visited door from run_scene locked_door_tiles. Moving units also derive draw order from unit_world_positions so enemy move tweens do not pop back at the end.

summary: Acolytes now drift forward on every intent and wardens step forward even on Bulwark turns so low-mobility enemies keep closing space without matching crawler speed.
details: The balance target is acolyte average toward-move 1.0 and warden average toward-move 1.5, both still below crawler's 1.75. tests/run_tests.gd locks this pacing so these archetypes stop corner camping without becoming rushdown enemies.

summary: Low-mobility enemy movement is now varied by intent: acolyte steps 2/1/3 for a two-tile average, while warden steps 1/0/2 for a one-tile average.
details: tests/run_tests.gd now checks per-intent movement variety plus simple per-intent averages, while still guarding that wardens remain slower than crawlers in weighted intent frequency.

summary: Ash floor rendering now uses seven extracted PNG variants chosen deterministically per room coordinate, with left/up neighbor de-clumping to avoid obvious repeats.
details: CombatBoardView loads res://assets/placeholders/tiles/base_floor_tile_01..07.png, trims each texture to its used rect, precomputes a _floor_variant_by_tile lookup in set_combat_state, and falls back to the first variant when indexing misses.

summary: Wall and door props now choose row-vs-column orientations from neighboring wall continuity; the perpendicular variant is a mirrored companion of the same processed base art.
details: Top/bottom runs use the base wall or door texture, side runs use a horizontal flip for exact style matching, and visible doors still render in the same tall prop frame as walls.

summary: Boundary wall corners should follow the later-drawn edge orientation, or mirrored wall segments visibly overhang at room corners.
details: CombatBoardView sorts board tiles by x+y and then x, so the corner fallback in _prop_orientation_variant needs to choose the edge that draws later rather than whichever boundary test runs first. The integrated door art also keeps the same trimmed footprint as wall.png so door tiles inherit the same tall prop frame without spilling past the tile.

summary: Room floors now generate as ash with deterministic moss accents, while _base_grid still consumes one legacy floor-theme roll so template and encounter RNG stay aligned with prior room seeds.
details: RoomGenerator applies moss after template stamping using a room-seeded coordinate hash plus light neighbor de-clumping, keeps entry tiles ash for readability, and never emits ember floor tiles from generation.

summary: Perimeter walls and doors now render as explicit boundary segments, and corner tiles split into two half-segments that meet at the tile center.
details: CombatBoardView no longer picks a single wall orientation per boundary tile. Straight perimeter tiles draw one full row or column segment, while corner tiles draw two cropped half-segments from the existing wall art so the outer runs meet cleanly in the middle of the corner tile without the old seam gap.

summary: Outer boundary wall and door art can stay fully implemented while the default board rendering collapses those edge tiles back to ash.
details: CombatBoardView keeps the boundary-segment wall/door helpers and tests, but OUTER_WALL_RENDERING_ENABLED is currently false, so _display_tile_id maps outer wall/door tiles to ash for presentation. This hides the perimeter blockers visually without changing the underlying grid passability or deleting the wall rendering code.

summary: Board props now use trimmed PNG art fitted bottom-center in tall tile frames, and visible doors reuse the wall-height prop frame.
details: This supports the new 255x255 wall, door, and pillar pixel-art assets without stretching them or rendering doors as low floor markers.

summary: Visible doors now render as standalone props with a dedicated frame instead of reusing wall-segment rendering.
details: CombatBoardView draws visible "door" tiles from the standalone door.png texture on their own centered frame, leaves the wall boundary-segment path for actual walls only, and reuses the same door sprite for every edge instead of mirroring wall-insert art. This replaced the older wall-height door treatment once the user swapped in a self-contained doorway asset.

summary: Door presentation now uses a cleaned transparent source plus skewed row/col variants derived from door.png for diagonal boundary exits.
details: The user-supplied door.png had an opaque fake checkerboard background, so the asset was cleaned to real alpha and used as the source/fallback door art. CombatBoardView now loads dedicated door_row.png and door_col.png transformed from that source and renders visible boundary doors through boundary_prop_segments again, so left/right edge doors follow the board perspective instead of reusing the same upright module everywhere.

summary: Door props slide toward each perimeter tile's mirrored back edge.
details: CombatBoardView offsets visible door frames by half a tile step toward the outside/back edge for all four perimeter sides: top-right up/right, bottom-right down/right, bottom-left down/left, and top-left up/left. Keep DOOR_BACK_EDGE_OFFSET_SCALE side-aware when retuning door placement so mirrored door orientations preserve the same apparent back-edge alignment.

summary: Permanent card upgrades keep base card ids and resolve through progression.
details: Card upgrade purchases are stored in progression.card_upgrades as base_card_id -> upgrade_id. Decks, rewards, analytics card ids, and saved runs keep base card ids; callers resolve display and combat behavior through GameData.card_def_with_upgrades/card_def_for_progression so collectible upgrades do not add those cards to the starting deck.

summary: Door opening animation slices door_opening.png as 8 row-major frames from a padded 4x2 sheet.
details: The source sheet is 1774x887, so CombatBoardView intentionally derives 443x443 frame cells by integer-dividing 4 columns by 2 rows and ignores the tiny right/bottom padding. Side-edge doors use horizontally flipped frame textures, matching the static door_col orientation.

summary: Labyrinth Crumble is generated from tools/build_labyrinth_font.py; regenerate font artifacts instead of hand-editing the TTF/TRES binaries.
details: The script emits fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-Regular.ttf, the embedded Godot FontFile .tres, and fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-preview.png from deterministic pixel glyph plans. The imagegen concept sheet is preserved as fonts/LabyrinthCrumble-reference.png for art direction.

summary: CombatBoardView board zoom now fits rendered tiles instead of the raw hidden-wall grid.
details: The board layout uses the extents of _tiles_in_draw_order() so hidden outer walls no longer make the room look smaller. Tile width can grow to 190px, and _board_origin biases the fitted content upward while preserving top clearance for unit HUDs and bottom clearance above the hand.

summary: Keep CardWidget compact cutoff below normal hand width
details: Combat hand cards normally max at 160px wide, so treating 160px as compact makes the icon summary rows render small. The rarity footer is hidden to reserve vertical space for larger icon rows.

summary: Board-wide overlays should target board_content_global_rect rather than CombatBoardView.size.
details: CombatBoardView fills the entire StageRoot, while the rendered isometric tiles occupy a much smaller cached footprint. DeathEngulfOverlay uses board_content_global_rect() so full-board visual effects grow from the actual tile bounds instead of covering the whole stage immediately.
archived_reason: DeathEngulfOverlay was changed to start from the full screen edge, so it no longer targets CombatBoardView.board_content_global_rect().

summary: Generated PNG overhaul intentionally leaves character art references untouched.
details: Non-character card, icon, relic, tile loot, and UI chrome assets now live under assets/art as generated PNGs. Remaining SVG references under assets/placeholders/units are intentional because the user explicitly asked not to replace player, enemy, or NPC character art during this overhaul.

summary: Enemy placeholder SVGs for harrier and warden now resolve to generated transparent PNG unit art.
details: data/enemies.json points Bone Harrier and Ash Warden at assets/placeholders/units/harrier.png and warden.png. Heart Warden remains on heart_warden.svg by request because the boss is planned for a ground-up redesign; NPC/player SVG placeholders were not part of this enemy-only art pass.

summary: Harrier and warden enemy PNG art now include same-stem 8-frame idle sheets.
details: data/enemies.json points Bone Harrier and Ash Warden at assets/placeholders/units/harrier.png and warden.png. Their idle animation sheets live at harrier_idle.png and warden_idle.png as 4x2 row-major atlases with 1020x1020 frames; CombatBoardView auto-loads same-stem _idle sheets with the default layout. Heart Warden remains on heart_warden.svg by request because the boss is planned for a ground-up redesign.

summary: Harrier and warden idle sheets are generated pose animations, not static bob sheets.
details: assets/placeholders/units/harrier_idle.png and warden_idle.png are 4x2 row-major 1020px-frame atlases generated through imagegen, then component-extracted, chroma-keyed, hard-alpha cleaned, globally palette-normalized, and baseline-aligned. The sheets intentionally contain real weight-shift pose changes with feet anchored rather than simple translations of the static PNGs.

summary: Harrier and warden generated idle sheets were pruned into slower ping-pong loops to avoid jitter.
details: The raw imagegen 8-frame sheets looked spasm-y because the generated frames were unordered pose variants with inconsistent silhouette motion. The current harrier_idle.png and warden_idle.png keep only the most compatible generated poses, duplicate/reorder them into calmer ping-pong loops, and data/enemies.json sets both enemies to idle_frame_seconds 0.18. This is a salvage pass rather than a fully clean hand-authored animation; avoid restoring all raw generated frames unless regenerating from scratch.

summary: Harrier and warden keep static PNG art but intentionally have no idle sheets.
details: The generated imagegen idle animation experiment was removed because even the salvaged ping-pong loops were not good enough to keep. CombatBoardView auto-loads same-stem _idle sheets, so harrier_idle.png and warden_idle.png should remain absent until a better third-party-generated spritesheet is available; data/enemies.json now has no idle_frame_seconds overrides for those enemies.

summary: CombatBoardView shadows are procedural ground-plane polygons.
details: Character shadows derive from each unit draw rect's planted bottom edge and use skewed isometric ground polygons. Tall prop shadows for pillars, doors, walls, and scene props are drawn immediately before the prop art in tile draw order so shadows sit on already-rendered floors while units and foreground props can still draw over them.

summary: CombatBoardView unit shadows use alpha-silhouette projection.
details: Unit shadows are based on AssetLoader.build_alpha_polygons for the current unit texture or idle AtlasTexture frame, cached per texture instance, then projected from the sprite's planted foot point onto the isometric ground. Generic ground ellipses are only a fallback; pillars, doors, walls, and scene props still use procedural ground-plane shadows drawn before the prop art.

summary: CombatBoardView unit shadow anchors use opaque sprite bounds.
details: Silhouette shadow data stores both alpha polygons and their opaque bounds. Normalize polygon points around the opaque bounds, scale by the opaque draw size, and anchor at the opaque-foot point inside the drawn texture rect; do not anchor shadows to draw_rect.end because generated unit sheets include transparent bottom padding. Height cast is slightly leftward to avoid making asymmetric silhouettes read horizontally flipped.

summary: CardWidget art sits on one continuous parchment frame with wrapped icon rows.
details: The current card frame uses assets/art/ui/card_frame.png as a texture stylebox while ArtFrame and DetailsPanel stay visually empty, so card art floats in the upper third and ability details share the parchment below. Keep dense icon-summary rows split into short segments; otherwise larger 26px ability icons can overflow narrow card interiors. The rarity indicator is now a visible bottom notch, so do not reserve vertical space by hiding rarity UI.

summary: Relic rooms present their cache through board scene props and bottom icon choices.
details: Treasure rooms add a relic_chest scene prop at Vector2i(4,4) in RunScene presentation, drawn by CombatBoardView using assets/art/tiles/ember_cache.png with aspect-preserving scene-prop sizing. Relic choices are stage overlays in RunScene rather than bottom ChoiceBar buttons, and claimed relic HUD frames carry relic_id metadata for acquisition pulse animations.

summary: Column torch fixtures render as paired pillar overlays.
details: CombatBoardView loads column_torch_left/right PNGs through _prop_textures and draws both after pillar moss so each visible isometric pillar face gets its own side-oriented hanging fixture. Placement is tuned through COLUMN_TORCH_* constants and should remain side-specific rather than mirroring one generic front-facing torch.

summary: Column torches are compact open-flame shaft-mounted overlays.
details: column_torch_left/right are short bracketed torch PNGs, not hanging braziers; CombatBoardView keeps them compact with COLUMN_TORCH_WIDTH_SCALE around 0.24 and anchors the mounting plate on the pillar's central masonry shaft below the cap. Future animated versions can replace these PNGs with matching side-oriented frames without reintroducing chains, bowls, or cap-spanning fixtures.

summary: Wood UI buttons use native-ratio sizing
details: assets/art/ui/button_wood_gold_*.png are 96x32, so UiSkin.button_native_size/apply_button_native_size keep wood-button controls at a 3:1 minimum size and opt them out of container fill stretching. Pass, Skip, and Cancel use the large action height so combat action controls stay 180x60 instead of shrinking to text width.

summary: Wood UI buttons now use raised 4.5:1 sprites
details: button_wood_gold_*.png are crisp 216x48 raised-button sprites with normal/hover/pressed states; pressed shifts content down by 3px and uses a darker depressed texture. UiSkin.BUTTON_TEXTURE_ASPECT is 4.5, Pass/Skip/Cancel use the large action height and remain left-aligned in the combat choice bar, while main-menu buttons use slimmer 216x48 sizing.

summary: Ambient elemental room particles use raster atlases with a separate blurred glow atlas rather than procedural shapes.
details: Atlas layout is 4 columns x 5 rows in assets/art/effects/ambient_particles.png and ambient_particles_glow.png, with rows ordered fire, ice, lightning, air, earth. Tune AMBIENT_PARTICLE_DENSITY, AMBIENT_PARTICLE_OPACITY, and AMBIENT_PARTICLE_SPEED_SCALE before changing sprite art.

summary: Ambient elemental room particles use raster atlases, with air wisps using path-reveal animation frames.
details: Base/glow elemental atlases are 4 columns x 5 rows in assets/art/effects/ambient_particles.png and ambient_particles_glow.png, with rows ordered fire, ice, lightning, air, earth. Air wisps additionally use 16-frame x 4-variant sheets ambient_air_wisp_frames.png and ambient_air_wisp_glow_frames.png so each wisp writes on and erases along its own curved alpha path. Tune AMBIENT_PARTICLE_DENSITY, AMBIENT_PARTICLE_OPACITY, and AMBIENT_PARTICLE_SPEED_SCALE before changing sprite art.

summary: CardWidget title base sizes are intentionally smaller.
details: Card title fitting now starts at 15/16/17 for compact/hand/full widths instead of 17/18/19, with the existing dynamic shrink path still able to go down to TITLE_MIN_SIZE. This keeps longer card names inside the nameplate without per-card title overrides.

summary: CardWidget title sizes use post-fit relief and a 15 pt render cap.
details: Card titles still search from the normal 17/18/19 fitting range, but the chosen fit is rendered 2 points smaller and capped at 15 pt via TITLE_FIT_RELIEF and TITLE_MAX_RENDER_SIZE. Lowering only base sizes was not reliable because long names that already fit at 17 could remain visually unchanged.

summary: CardWidget title fitting targets the visual nameplate width.
details: Card titles now evaluate rendered font sizes against a visual nameplate-safe width (TITLE_NAMEPLATE_WIDTH_RATIO) instead of the full Label width, then apply the 2 pt relief and 15 pt cap. This keeps medium names like Bodkin Arrow at 15 pt while shrinking wider names such as Ricochet Knife, Rallying Breath, and Firebrand Volley enough to stay inside the visible plaque.

summary: Ambient elemental particles use raster atlases; air wisps animate through 32 path-reveal frames and ice is tuned as fine white snowfall.
details: Base/glow elemental atlases are 4 columns x 5 rows in assets/art/effects/ambient_particles.png and ambient_particles_glow.png, rows fire, ice, lightning, air, earth. Air wisps use 32-frame x 4-variant sheets ambient_air_wisp_frames.png and ambient_air_wisp_glow_frames.png with faster per-particle phase speeds so each wisp writes on and erases along its curved alpha path without obvious frame stepping. Ice keeps the base atlas but its row is whitened, the renderer draws it at smaller width scales, and ice has a higher base count for denser snowfall.

summary: Ambient elemental particles use raster atlases; fire is softened with a blurred mote layer, air uses 32 path-reveal frames, and ice is fine white snowfall.
details: Base/glow elemental atlases are 4 columns x 5 rows in assets/art/effects/ambient_particles.png and ambient_particles_glow.png, rows fire, ice, lightning, air, earth. Fire additionally uses ambient_fire_soft_particles.png and draws glow/trail/soft layers with only a faint scaled-down crisp core so embers do not read as flat sprites. Air wisps use 32-frame x 4-variant sheets ambient_air_wisp_frames.png and ambient_air_wisp_glow_frames.png. Ice keeps the base atlas but its row is whitened, drawn smaller, and given a higher base count for denser snowfall.

summary: Ambient elemental particles use raster atlases with fire motes drawn from a separate soft atlas at half-size.
details: Fire rooms use assets/art/effects/ambient_fire_soft_particles.png for blurred ember body/glow layers, then draw a very faint base atlas core. The fire draw scale is intentionally 0.085-0.16 tile width, about half the original 0.17-0.32, while the soft atlas has a boosted mid-alpha curve so small particles still read without looking like flat PNGs. Air uses 32 path-reveal frames and ice uses small white snowfall.

summary: Ambient elemental particles use raster atlases with fire motes drawn from a separate soft atlas at quarter-size.
details: Fire rooms use assets/art/effects/ambient_fire_soft_particles.png for blurred ember body/glow layers, then draw a very faint base atlas core. The fire draw scale is intentionally 0.0425-0.08 tile width, one quarter of the original 0.17-0.32, while the soft atlas has a boosted mid-alpha curve so the tiny particles still read without looking like flat PNGs. Air uses 32 path-reveal frames and ice uses small white snowfall.

summary: Ambient elemental particles use raster atlases with fire and air softened by separate blurred body layers.
details: Fire rooms use assets/art/effects/ambient_fire_soft_particles.png for blurred ember body/glow layers, then draw a very faint base atlas core at 0.0425-0.08 tile width. Air rooms preserve the 32-frame path-reveal timing from ambient_air_wisp_frames.png but now draw ambient_air_wisp_soft_frames.png as the main blurred body, the glow atlas as trail/halo, and the original wisp frame only as a faint crisp core at the same draw scale. Ice uses small white snowfall.

summary: UI probes must clear saved runs and load a fresh deterministic run state before capturing; otherwise screenshots can silently reuse stale progress and mask changes like enemy-density or HUD updates.
Combat action controls reserve a stable left column width.
details: RunScene computes the left action column from two large native action buttons plus the ChoiceBar gap and padding. Keep this width reserved while piles/action choices are visible so moving from Pass to Skip/Cancel during card targeting does not reflow the hand row.

summary: Melee combat VFX uses a generated transparent slash sprite.
details: assets/art/effects/melee_slash.png is a chroma-key-removed imagegen asset loaded by CombatBoardView as res://assets/art/effects/melee_slash.png. Keep melee effect polish in this raster asset plus draw sizing/rotation rather than returning to procedural crossed lines.

summary: Campfire room actions now use a StageRoot context overlay instead of the bottom choice bar.
details: RunScene builds ContextChoiceOverlay dynamically under StageRoot and routes campfire Sit/Leave there via _add_context_choice_button; other modes still use BottomStack/ChoiceBar.

summary: Foreground obstruction fading is entry-based across board contents.
details: CombatBoardView builds obstruction entries from visible units, scene props, destructible terrain, loot, and traps. Tall foreground props (walls, pillars, doors, scene props, terrain) use those entries to fade when overlapping earlier-drawn board contents, not just characters.

summary: Campfire choices use relic-style panels.
details: RunScene now presents campfire choices through the shared RelicChoiceOverlay instead of ContextChoiceOverlay buttons. Linger for a moment calls RunEngine.leave_campfire with a 10 HP heal and continues; Embrace the fire's warmth keeps the old fire-rest banking/unlock flow, showing ??? until rested_at_fire/card_upgrades_unlocked is true.

summary: Enemy advance movement is route-scored, while threat previews show full reach.
details: move_toward evaluates all actually reachable anchors, avoids traps, scores by remaining route to the target, and uses destructible terrain only as a planning hint so enemies can move up to blockers before attack actions break them. enemy_threat_tiles intentionally previews full movement reach and all attack tiles from the movement frontier instead of filtering by whether each move gets closer to the current player tile.

summary: Enemy threat previews mirror full movement, footprints, and special attacks.
details: enemy_threat_tiles routes movement endpoints into attack previews for melee, ranged, aoe, push, pull, and lightning_strikes. Attack previews build a temporary enemy at each anchor so large footprints such as Zekarion threaten from every occupied square; lightning_strikes previews use the deterministic _lightning_strike_tiles result instead of hiding or overgeneralizing the special attack.

summary: Enemy threat previews assume the player may vacate their current tile.
details: enemy_threat_tiles uses a threat-only blocker set that erases the current player position while preserving terrain, traps, enemies, and illusions. This keeps red threat zones conservative for move/blink destinations: if the player merely relocates without opening or closing paths, enemy movement previews include routes through the old player tile so destinations they can hit are marked.

summary: Elemental enemy reach budgets preserve movement safety.
details: Air room enemies keep their +1 movement at medium/deep encounter depths, but elementalized attacks are fixed to range 3 so their max normal-roster move+attack reach is 8 instead of 9. Lightning room enemies keep high attack ranges, but positive move_toward/move_away actions lose 1 tile with a floor of 1 so their max normal-roster reach is 6.

summary: Manual headless console mirrors real input: click/card plays printed text; drag play|attack|move models UI lanes, including fallback attack 2 and move 2. Notes and analytics stay under the chosen output dir.

Runtime orientation is stored only on resolved action copies: orientation for rotatable AOE, force_direction for push/pull. Analytics play-mode comparisons erase those fields so printed cards stay classified as printed.
Turn-order animation uses staged FLIP reflow
details: The turn-order widget intentionally removes entries by sliding/fading them upward while their slot remains, rebuilds the final order, inverts surviving portraits from their old global positions so only the relevant entries slide into place, then fades/drops inserted entries into the opened slot. Avoid reverting to custom_minimum_size collapse/expand because that reads like a static reorder instead of a game-style queue update.

summary: Card time now uses a 1-10 scale with baseline 5.
details: Printed player cards now use a wider initiative-time curve: fast cards are around 1-3, normal cards around 5, and heavy commitments around 8-10. Runtime scheduling remains current_clock + player_base_initiative + total card time, so two average cards make card time roughly as important as the base delay while Agility still matters. The card heuristic baseline is 5 with a 0.45 tempo delta.

summary: CardWidget preview sizes must preserve the native card aspect
details: CardWidget now scales margins, title bands, art/details bands, fonts, time badges, and summary icons from one uniform card scale based on the native 250x352 card. RunScene card surfaces should hand CardWidget rectangles normalized to the 352/250 aspect so draw/discard piles, hand cards, tooltips, equipment previews, and upgrade previews do not stretch frames, gems, art, or action rows independently.

summary: Equipment tile loot needs a distinct pickup marker
details: Raw 96x96 transparent equipment icons shrink to a dark 58px object on ash floor tiles and are easy to miss. CombatBoardView should keep equipment pickups larger than consumables and draw a rarity/accent-backed pickup marker behind the actual icon so drops are visibly distinct without replacing the gear art.
archived_reason: User rejected the crude marker/shape treatment for equipment tile loot; equipment should render as the actual icon with normal pickup placement and shadow.

summary: Equipment re-equip animations use a dedicated gear FX layer
details: Character-sheet equipment drag/drop animations should render temporary icon proxies on EquipmentFxLayer above the character overlay. Do not use CardFxLayer for these room-mode UI animations because RunScene clears CardFxLayer outside combat/reward, which can erase snap/swap proxies during overlay rebuilds.

summary: Equipment re-equip drag uses in-scene proxies instead of native Control DnD
details: Character-sheet equipment drag should be handled by RunScene with EquipmentHeldProxy/EquipmentSwapProxy controls on EquipmentFxLayer. Avoid Godot native Control drag/drop for gear: its OS cursor feedback can show a forbidden-circle cursor and obscure the intended held-item presentation. The dedicated gear FX layer also avoids CardFxLayer cleanup outside combat/reward.

summary: Character menu card badges reuse card art
details: Gear/Magic deck badges, Magic loadout tiles, and the held magic proxy now reuse each card's art_path as a cropped horizontal background with a dark wash and accent strip, rather than maintaining separate badge assets. New card art should keep a recognizable cue in the central y≈48..96 source band so the character-menu crop reads well.

summary: Character menu card badges use soft accent tint, not hard strips
details: Gear/Magic deck badges, Magic loadout tiles, and the held magic proxy crop each card's art_path behind the name. The inner wash should use a faint full-surface accent tint plus dark readability wash; avoid hard left/bottom accent strips because they read as crude overlapping lines. The colored border carries the explicit accent.

summary: Character menu card badges fill transparent art edges with muted backing
details: Gear/Magic deck badges, Magic loadout tiles, and held magic proxies now put ElementData.card_art_background plus a dim overscanned copy of the card art behind the sharp art crop, then apply the dark readability wash and label. This avoids black side gutters from ragged transparent card art while preserving the no-hard-strips visual direction.

summary: Parallel Codex task workflow uses isolated worktrees and temp-HOME Godot runs
details: Labyrinth parallel task infrastructure lives in .codex/skills/parallel-labyrinth-task plus tools/parallel_task.py, tools/godot_task_runner.py, and tools/visual_probe_runner.py. Godot commands should run through the wrappers so each process gets a task-local HOME under /private/tmp/labyrinth-godot-home, a safe --log-file, and LABYRINTH_TASK_ID; setting LABYRINTH_TASK_ID without a temp HOME/log file can crash or fail under the sandbox when Godot rotates user:// logs before the runtime hook can create directories.

summary: Orchestration requests authorize visible background threads
details: For Labyrinth queue orchestration, a request to use -labyrinth-tasks, run queued work, launch workers, start background tasks, or parallelize the queue is enough permission to create user-visible Codex app/background threads. Do not make the user separately say 'create background threads' each time; still stop if the host session does not expose create/read/send app-thread tools.

summary: Initiative balance now favors standard early player returns
details: Player base initiative is 9 with Agility reducing it to a floor of 5. Starter card times now average about 4.1; Whirlwind Slash is normal-speed at 5 and Bloody Lunge is the heavy starter at 8. First-sequence weighted repeat cycles are about wisp 11, crawler 13, harrier 13.4, acolyte 16.25, warden 20.25, and Zekarion 19.25, so normal two-card starter turns should usually return before the same fast enemy follows up while heavy+normal turns can let fast enemies double-up.

summary: Initiative balance now uses intent-aware first enemy timing and a wider fast-card pool
details: Initial enemy queue slots now use enemy base initiative plus revealed intent time, with only an enemy-index stagger for readability; repeats already used the same base+intent cycle. Player base initiative remains 9 with Agility floor 5. The June 2026 speed rebalance broadened card times so the starting deck averages about 3.56 time, the full card pool has 32 cards at time 1-3, and reward-eligible cards include time-2 Threaded Path, time-3 Stone Plate, and eleven time-4 options. Practical pacing target: two fast cards return around initiative 13 and can lap slower enemies, two medium cards return around 18 without fast enemy double-ups, and two slow cards around 23 can let wisps/crawlers threaten doubles.

summary: Generated traps are a high-value positional payoff
details: Trap damage is intentionally tuned above weak direct ranged attacks: first-sequence local depths deal 6/7/8 player-scale damage, boss-depth traps deal 9, and later sequences add 2 per completed sequence. Status payloads still use local encounter depth so early fire/poison traps keep shallow pressure.

summary: Campfire bonfire alpha cleanup is baked into PNG assets
details: CombatBoardView draws assets/art/tiles/campfire_bonfire.png and campfire_bonfire_idle.png directly; no runtime alpha cleanup is applied to the campfire prop, and no unaltered animation source is checked in. Future repairs should use frame-local exterior flood-fill to preserve border-connected transparency while filling only enclosed low-alpha islands inside the flame/smoke artwork.

summary: Main menu title gradient avoids screen-space shaders
details: The title face is implemented with fine clipped Label bands under TitleFaceBlend. A ShaderMaterial using FRAGCOORD produced a smooth fill in code but visual probes on macOS display scaling made most of the title render too dark, so future title-face polish should prefer the clipped-label ramp unless the shader can use stable local text coordinates.

summary: Combat room entry now pauses on a visual pre-battle preview
details: RunScene simulates move_to_room on a duplicated room-mode run state to build the pre-battle enemy/deck/loadout preview without sealing or moving rooms. The Start button calls _on_map_view_room_selected with skip_pre_battle=true to use the normal transition/analytics path, and the preview stays below the character overlay so equipment or magic swaps can update the preview before combat starts.

summary: Elemental enemy reach budgets preserve movement safety.
details: Air room enemies keep their +1 movement at medium/deep encounter depths, but elementalized attacks stay in a 3-4 range band so their max normal-roster move+attack reach is 8 instead of 9. Lightning room enemies keep high attack ranges, but positive move_toward/move_away actions lose 1 tile with a floor of 1 so their max normal-roster reach is 6.

summary: Depth-two fire rooms keep shallow burn pressure
details: Early playtest runs repeatedly died to depth-two fire burn spirals before reaching the first boss. Fire enemy attacks now use a one-player-scale burn payload at encounter depths 1-2 and only restore the heavier burn payload at deeper standard rooms, while keeping the direct fire damage bump at depth 2.

summary: Depth-two fire traps keep shallow burn pressure
details: Fire traps now apply one-player-scale burn at depths 1-2 and reserve the heavier burn payload for deeper fire rooms, matching the combat-engine fire enemy burn ramp used after early playtest deaths from depth-two burn attrition.
archived_reason: Fire trap shallow-burn tuning remains, but it no longer matches a combat-engine fire enemy burn ramp because enemy room-element attack rewriting was removed.

summary: Equipment pickups use a warm visibility beacon
details: Room equipment drops intentionally render larger and raised above the tile with a warm pickup glow blended with rarity accent; pure rarity tint made common grey gear blend back into ash floors.

summary: Equipment tile loot uses icon-only pickup rendering
details: User rejected the hand-drawn marker/plate/circle treatment for equipment pickups. Equipment loot should render as the actual equipment icon with the normal loot ground shadow and the same bottom-anchored tile footprint as potion and shield pickups; visibility should be solved by reliable drop placement/rates, not extra board shapes.

summary: Committed saves stay ahead of combat presentation
details: RunScene holds the newest coherent run snapshot separately while card, room-travel, and enemy animations render local before/after states; _committed_run_state and close paths must prefer that hold so animation-time quits cannot roll back. CombatEngine commit steps belong before each enemy mutation's presentation and must carry the post-action rng_state plus initiative/turn checkpoints. Never serialize hover, selection, drag, or animation presentation state.

summary: Record run results inside terminal checkpoint finalization
details: The committed-boundary save path can finalize and clear victory/defeat before the later recap hooks run. _finalize_terminal_committed_state must call _terminal_state_with_recorded_run_result first and adopt its embedded progression before banking/loss processing and save_data; the durable result ledger makes reload retries idempotent.
archived_reason: Redundant with the existing terminal-state persistence decision.

summary: Clicked combat cards default directly to their printed action
details: Do not put a mandatory mode-choice click between selecting a card and using its printed action. A click should immediately enter normal printed targeting while a persistent mode-tab row defaults to CARD; optional fallback tabs may retarget the same card and must display their live values, such as ATTACK 20 and MOVE 2, with unavailable modes visibly disabled.

summary: Flurry snapshots card plays before resolution
details: Cards with top-level flurry:true expand their printed actions once per card play available when the printed play begins. The commit spends that snapshotted count and multiplies printed time and health cost by it; card-play bonuses or kill refunds earned during repeated actions are not folded back into the repeat count and remain available afterward. Fallback Attack/Move modes do not inherit Flurry.

summary: Flurry cards earn value from copies, not printed rate
details: Keep Flurry's individual printed action package deliberately weak and showcase flexible hybrid utility rather than an attack-only cycle. Useful roles include block plus attack, elemental intensity plus attack, draw plus attack, and movement plus attack; the copied two-play result and single-card/single-Time compression are the payoff.

summary: Flurry icon must not resemble the Draw stack
details: Avoid upright fans or stacks of three complete cards because Draw already uses that silhouette. Prefer a single large landscape card moving sideways with compact afterimage trails, while preserving the dark-fantasy parchment, ink, crimson, and gold icon style and checking it at native CardWidget size.

summary: Loadout notifications use per-category durable unread ids
details: New equipment/items append to unread_loadout_equipment and new reward/merchant spells append to unread_loadout_magic. RunScene derives both the header count and Gear/Magic tab badges from these arrays, and clears only the category whose character tab was opened so save/resume and mixed acquisitions stay honest.

summary: Card motion should be continuous, readable, and physically staged
details: Played cards should use one persistent proxy from hand through a modest grow into center, a readable hold, and a smooth shrinking flight into the destination pile; do not fade/release and respawn between those legs. Play, draw, discard, consume, and snapback should favor continuous zero-speed-endpoint easing over segmented Back-eased tweens. Multi-card draws should overlap with a short stagger and remain in their fan slots until the authoritative hand refresh replaces them.

summary: StageRoot must clip the navigable combat board
details: CombatBoardView custom drawing is not clipped by the board Control's own clip_contents setting. Keep Backdrop/Margin/MainVBox/StageRoot.clip_contents enabled so zoomed or panned tiles cannot paint over the top HUD or hand; the board's clip_contents still clips its dynamic child layer.
